## Idea

The **Milstein scheme** simulates the solution of an SDE (see
[[sde-simulation]]) and improves on the [[euler-maruyama-method]] by keeping
one more term of the stochastic Taylor expansion. Consider

$$
dX_t=f(t,X_t)\,dt+g(t,X_t)\,dW_t,
$$

with Lipschitz coefficients $f,g$ and [[brownian-motion]] $W$, simulated on
the grid $t_n=n\Delta t$ with $\Delta W_n=W_{t_{n+1}}-W_{t_n}$. Euler-Maruyama
freezes $g$ at the left endpoint. Applying the [[ito-formula]] to $g$ instead
shows the next-largest term is $L^1g\int\!\!\int dW\,dW$, where
$L^1=g\,\partial_x$, and the double integral is explicit,

$$
\int_{t_n}^{t_{n+1}}\int_{t_n}^{s}dW_u\,dW_s
=\tfrac{1}{2}\left((\Delta W_n)^2-\Delta t\right).
$$

## The Scheme

:::{.definition data-title="Milstein Scheme"}

$$
X_{n+1}=X_n+f(t_n,X_n)\Delta t+g(t_n,X_n)\Delta W_n
+\frac{1}{2}\,g(t_n,X_n)\,\partial_xg(t_n,X_n)
\left((\Delta W_n)^2-\Delta t\right).
$$

:::

The extra term is a correction for the fact that the diffusion coefficient
changes across the step, and it vanishes when $g$ does not depend on $x$
(additive noise), in which case Milstein coincides with Euler-Maruyama.

## Example: Black-Scholes-Merton Model

For the [[black-scholes-merton-model|BSM model]] under $\mathbb{Q}$,
$f=rS$ and $g=\sigma S$, so $g\,\partial_xg=\sigma^2S$. Writing
$\Delta W=\sqrt{\Delta t}\,\xi$ with $\xi\sim\mathcal{N}(0,1)$,

$$
S_{t+\Delta t}=S_t\left\{1+\sigma\sqrt{\Delta t}\,\xi
+\Delta t\left[r+\tfrac{1}{2}\sigma^2(\xi^2-1)\right]\right\}.
$$

This is easy to simulate with a loop, where `h` is the step size.

```
S <- S0
for (i in 2:length(t)) {
  xi <- rnorm(1, 0, 1)
  S[i] <- S[i-1] * (1 + sigma * sqrt(h) * xi +
            h * (r + 0.5 * sigma^2 * (xi^2 - 1)))
}
```

## Convergence

To compare the two schemes one measures the error $X_n\to X(t_n)$ in the
strong sense, $\mathbb{E}|X_n-X(t_n)|$, and in the weak sense,
$|\mathbb{E}\,\phi(X_n)-\mathbb{E}\,\phi(X(t_n))|$. Under the usual smoothness
assumptions Milstein has strong order $1$, against order $1/2$ for
Euler-Maruyama, while both have weak order $1$. The comparison is carried out
in [[sde-simulation]].
